correctness.rationale: Invariant-measure testing against arbitrary antiderivatives of \(y\) gives \(\mathbb E[x\mid y]=0\), and testing against arbitrary antiderivatives of \(z\) gives \(\mathbb E[x^2\mid z]=1\). The thermostat equation then gives the exact variance defect. Zero defect would force \(x^2=1\) on compact invariant support; continuity makes \(x\) constant on each support trajectory, while \(\dot y=x\) makes \(y\) unbounded, a contradiction. Mean \(x^2=1\) plus strict variance forces positive mass on both sides of \(|x|=1\). Krylov–Bogolyubov averaging transfers the measure statement to every nonempty compact invariant set. The packaged checker verifies the residual and variance algebra.

originality.rationale: The known scalar balance \(\langle x^2\rangle=1\), zero mean thermostat friction, and repeated crossing of \(z=0\) were located explicitly in prior same-object literature and removed from the originality claim. The full 1985 primary article gives the equations and canonical stationary density; the full 2011 mathematical paper studies Darboux integrability; the full 2019 paper develops global moment identities and the z=0 result; invariant-torus papers study orbit geometry. None of the inspected same-object sources states or implication-wise supplies the all-invariant-measures conditional law \(\mathbb E[x^2\mid z]=1\), its infinite orthogonality family, or the strict \(|x|=1\) compact-recurrence crossing theorem. Published semantic-index searches over direct and equivalent formulations returned only trigonometric-model or distinct-system analogues.
residual_risks: The 1986 stability/order/chaos article was compared through its publisher abstract rather than a complete locally searchable copy.
The 2015 invariant-tori source was compared through its published abstract rather than complete full text.

The canonical Gaussian stationary density trivially has the conditional law by independence, so an older statistical-mechanics discussion could have observed the same identity for that one measure without extending it to every compact invariant measure.
The accepted generator proof is short enough that an equivalent all-invariant-measures statement could remain in unindexed thermostat literature.

No novelty is claimed for the Nosé–Hoover equations, global target-temperature average, zero mean friction, z=0 crossing theorem, canonical stationary density, nonergodicity, invariant tori, or known integrability results.

value.rationale: The defining purpose of the Nosé–Hoover thermostat is to regulate kinetic temperature, while the classical one-oscillator model is famously nonergodic and decomposes into periodic, quasiperiodic, and chaotic components. The accepted theorem shows that thermostat calibration survives this decomposition much more strongly than the known global average suggests: every compact invariant component has target kinetic temperature separately on every thermostat-variable fiber. The strict variance defect quantifies unavoidable thermostat activity, and the resulting \(|x|=1\) crossing theorem gives a finite-amplitude geometric constraint on every compact recurrent state. These facts are natural diagnostics for invariant-torus or periodic-orbit computations and directly connect the thermostat's statistical purpose to the oscillator's nonergodic dynamics.
